You are doing a read-only audit review of the OpenZeppelin Stylus contracts library. You must NOT modify any file inside /private/tmp/bench/ws or any worktree under /tmp/bench/wt. Write your outputs only under /tmp/bench/notes/.

Inputs:
- Audit reports (PDF, in the repo at /private/tmp/bench/ws/audits/):
  "2024-10-v0.1.0.pdf", "Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit.pdf", "Stylus Contracts Library v0.3.0 Audit.pdf"
  Read them with the Read tool using the `pages` parameter (max 20 pages per request). Read every page.
- The v0.3.0 code, which is the baseline: /tmp/bench/wt/v030 (a detached git worktree at tag v0.3.0). Use it for all code reads. Read-only commands only (grep, sed, cat, git show).

Task:
1. Extract EVERY finding from all three reports into a table. Columns: report, finding ID, title, severity as the auditor rated it, the auditor's status (resolved / acknowledged / partially resolved / unresolved / not stated), the auditor's description in one or two sentences, and the fix commit or PR if the report gives one.
2. For every finding the report marks as resolved (or fixed, or similar), verify on the v0.3.0 code that it is REALLY fixed. Find the code that implements the fix (file path and line range in /tmp/bench/wt/v030). Read it. Decide one verdict: FIXED (the fix addresses the root cause and the auditor's reproduction would fail), PARTIAL (fixed for the reported instance but the same issue remains elsewhere, name the place), NOT FIXED (the code still has the issue), or CANNOT VERIFY (say why). Give the evidence: file:line and a one or two sentence reasoning. Do not trust the report's word for it.
3. For findings that are acknowledged or unresolved in the v0.3.0 report, state whether the issue still exists in v0.3.0 code (same verdict scheme).
4. Write the table and the verdicts to /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Keep it accurate and concise. Do not invent findings. If a PDF page is unreadable, say so.

Your final message is a short summary (at most 25 lines): counts per report by verdict, and the list of resolved findings that you judge NOT FIXED or PARTIAL, with their file paths.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Read

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. 1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.
69	
70	## Git
71	- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
72	  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
73	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
74	- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
75	  or any command that touches other worktrees.
76	
77	## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
78	- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
79	- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
80	- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
81	  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
82	- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
83	- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).
51

18	    /// This module provides the cryptographic primitives needed for the

20	    /// ECDSA signature and message hash.
21	    ///
22	    /// Re-exports selected ECDSA types and constants specifically relevant
23	    /// to the ecrecover operation.
24	    pub mod ecrecover {
25	        pub use crate::utils::cryptography::ecdsa::{
26	            ECDSAInvalidSignature, ECDSAInvalidSignatureS, EcRecoverData,
27	            Error, ECRECOVER_ADDR, SIGNATURE_S_UPPER_BOUND,
28	        };
29	    }
30	}

32	/// Trait providing access to Arbitrum precompiles for Stylus contracts.
33	///
34	/// This trait wraps complex precompile invocations to provide a clean,
35	/// ergonomic interface for calling Arbitrum's built-in cryptographic functions
36	/// and utilities from within Stylus smart contracts.
37	///
38	/// Precompiles are pre-deployed contracts at fixed addresses that implement
39	/// commonly used cryptographic operations and other utilities. They execute
40	/// natively in the Arbitrum runtime for better performance compared to
41	/// implementing these operations in contract code.
42	///
43	/// See: <https://docs.arbitrum.io/build-decentralized-apps/precompiles/overview>
44	///
45	/// # Usage
46	///
47	/// Implement this trait for your contract storage type to gain access to
48	/// precompile functionality:
49	///
50	/// ```rust,ignore
51	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::utils::cryptography::Precompiles;
52	///
53	/// #[storage]
54	/// #[entrypoint]
55	/// struct MyContract {
56	///     // your fields...
57	/// }
58	///
59	/// // The `Precompiles` trait is automatically implemented for all
60	/// // contracts annotated with `#[entrypoint]` or that implement
61	/// // `stylus_sdk::prelude::TopLevelStorage`.
62	///
63	/// #[public]
64	/// impl MyContract {
65	///     fn verify_signature(&mut self, msg_hash: B256, sig: (u8, B256, B256)) -> Result<Address, Error> {
66	///         let (v, r, s) = sig;
67	///         self.ec_recover(msg_hash, v, r, s)
68	///     }
69	/// }
70	/// ```
71	///
72	/// # Error Handling
73	///
74	/// Precompile methods return `Result` types to handle both invalid inputs and
75	/// precompile execution failures. Always handle these errors appropriately
76	/// in your contract logic.
77	pub trait Precompiles: TopLevelStorage {
78	    /// Recovers the address that signed a hashed message (`hash`) using an
79	    /// ECDSA signature (v, r, s).
80	    ///
81	    /// Wrapper around the `ecRecover` precompile.
82	    ///
83	    /// # Arguments
84	    ///
85	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
86	    /// * `hash` - Hash of the message.
87	    /// * `v` - `v` value from the signature.
88	    /// * `r` - `r` value from the signature.
89	    /// * `s` - `s` value from the signature.
90	    ///
91	    /// # Errors
92	    ///
93	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignatureS`] - If the `s` value is grater than
94	    ///   [`primitives::ecrecover::SIGNATURE_S_UPPER_BOUND`].
95	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignature`] - If the recovered address is
96	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
97	    ///
98	    /// # Panics
99	    ///
100	    /// * If the `ecRecover` precompile fails to execute.
101	    fn ec_recover(
102	        &self,
103	        hash: B256,
104	        v: u8,
105	        r: B256,
106	        s: B256,
107	    ) -> Result<Address, Error>;
108	
109	    /// Performs signature verifications in the `secp256r1` elliptic curve.
110	    ///
111	    /// Wrapper around the `P256VERIFY` precompile introduced in [RIP-7212].
112	    ///
113	    /// [RIP-7212]: https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/blob/723155c3d86427412b5bc0f98ad1e4791ea7347f/RIPS/rip-7212.md
114	    ///
115	    /// # Arguments
116	    ///
117	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
118	    /// * `hash` - Signed data hash.
119	    /// * `r` - `r` component of the signature.
120	    /// * `s` - `s` component of the signature.
121	    /// * `x` - `x` coordinate of the public key.
122	    /// * `y` - `y` coordinate of the public key.
123	    fn p256_verify(
124	        &self,
125	        hash: B256,
126	        r: B256,
127	        s: B256,
128	        x: B256,
129	        y: B256,
130	    ) -> bool;
131	}
132	
133	impl<T: TopLevelStorage> Precompiles for T {
134	    fn ec_recover(
135	        &self,
136	        hash: B256,
137	        v: u8,
138	        r: B256,
139	        s: B256,
140	    ) -> Result<Address, Error> {
141	        recover(self, hash, v, r, s)
142	    }
143	
144	    fn p256_verify(
145	        &self,
146	        hash: B256,
147	        r: B256,
148	        s: B256,
149	        x: B256,
150	        y: B256,
151	    ) -> bool {
152	        p256_verify(self, hash, r, s, x, y)
153	    }
154	}

1	//! An upgradeability mechanism designed for UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy
2	//! Standard) proxies as defined in [ERC-1822].
3	//!
4	//! [ERC-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
5	//!
6	//! The functions included here can perform an upgrade of an
7	//! [`Erc1967Proxy`], when this contract is set as the implementation
8	//! behind such a proxy.
9	//!
10	//! [`Erc1967Proxy`]: crate::proxy::erc1967::Erc1967Proxy
11	
12	// The contract is covered 100% via e2e tests, but this cannot be displayed due
13	// to the inability llvm-cov to display e2e coverage. Marking this with
14	// coverage(off) to avoid a false negative.
15	//
16	// TODO: remove this attribute when 100% coverage can be achieved through unit
17	// tests.
18	#![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
19	
20	pub use alloc::{string::String, vec, vec::Vec};
21	
22	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B256, uint, Address, U256, U32};
23	use alloy_sol_types::SolCall;
24	pub use sol::*;
25	use stylus_sdk::{
26	    abi::Bytes,
27	    call::{Call, MethodError},
28	    prelude::*,
29	    storage::{StorageBool, StorageU32},
30	};
31	
32	use crate::{
33	    proxy::{
34	        erc1967::{
35	            self,
36	            utils::{
37	                ERC1967InvalidAdmin, ERC1967InvalidBeacon,
38	                ERC1967InvalidImplementation, ERC1967NonPayable, Erc1967Utils,
39	                IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT,
40	            },
41	        },
42	        utils::erc1822::{Erc1822ProxiableInterface, IErc1822Proxiable},
43	    },
44	    utils::{
45	        address::{self, AddressUtils},
46	        storage_slot::StorageSlot,
47	    },
48	};
49	
50	/// The version of the upgrade interface of the contract.
51	pub const UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION: &str = "5.0.0";
52	
53	/// The version number of the logic contract.
54	pub const VERSION_NUMBER: U32 = uint!(1_U32);
55	
56	/// A sentinel storage slot used by the implementation to distinguish
57	/// implementation vs. proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) execution
58	/// contexts.
59	///
60	/// The slot key is derived from `keccak256("Stylus.uups.logic.flag") - 1`,
61	/// chosen to avoid storage collisions with application state.
62	///
63	/// Behavior:
64	/// - When called directly on the implementation, `logic_flag == true`.
65	/// - When called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), `logic_flag ==
66	///   false` (i.e., the proxy’s storage does not contain this
67	///   implementation-only flag).
68	///
69	/// Security notes:
70	/// - This boolean flag replaces Solidity’s `immutable __self` pattern.
71	///
72	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
73	pub const LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT: B256 = {
74	    const HASH: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
75	        .update(b"Stylus.uups.logic.flag")
76	        .finalize();
77	    let slot = U256::from_be_bytes(HASH)
78	        .wrapping_sub(uint!(1_U256))
79	        .to_be_bytes::<32>();
80	
81	    B256::new(slot)
82	};
83	
84	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
85	mod sol {
86	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
87	
88	    sol! {
89	        /// The call is from an unauthorized context.
90	        #[derive(Debug)]
91	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
92	        error UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext();
93	
94	        /// The storage `slot` is unsupported as a UUID.
95	        ///
96	        /// * `slot` - The unsupported UUID returned by the implementation.
97	        #[derive(Debug)]
98	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
99	        error UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID(bytes32 slot);
100	
101	        /// The contract is already initialized.
102	        #[derive(Debug)]
103	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
104	        error InvalidInitialization();
105	
106	        /// The version is not greater than the current version.
107	        ///
108	        /// * `current_version` - The current version.
109	        #[derive(Debug)]
110	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
111	        error InvalidVersion(uint32 current_version);
112	
113	        interface UUPSUpgradeableInterface {
114	            function setVersion() external;
115	        }
116	    }
117	}
118	
119	/// An [`UUPSUpgradeable`] error.
120	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
121	pub enum Error {
122	    /// The call is from an unauthorized context.
123	    UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext),
124	    /// The storage `slot` is unsupported as a UUID.
125	    UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID),
126	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `implementation`
127	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
128	    InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation),
129	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `admin` of the
130	    /// proxy is invalid.
131	    InvalidAdmin(ERC1967InvalidAdmin),
132	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `beacon`
133	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
134	    InvalidBeacon(ERC1967InvalidBeacon),
135	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that an upgrade function
136	    /// sees [`stylus_sdk::msg::value()`] > [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]
137	    /// that may be lost.
138	    NonPayable(ERC1967NonPayable),
139	    /// There's no code at `target` (it is not a contract).
140	    EmptyCode(address::AddressEmptyCode),
141	    /// A call to an address target failed. The target may have reverted.
142	    FailedCall(address::FailedCall),
143	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the
144	    /// [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] failed.
145	    FailedCallWithReason(address::FailedCallWithReason),
146	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the contract is already
147	    /// initialized.
148	    InvalidInitialization(InvalidInitialization),
149	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the version is not greater
150	    /// than the current version.
151	    InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion),
152	}
153	
154	impl From<erc1967::utils::Error> for Error {
155	    fn from(e: erc1967::utils::Error) -> Self {
156	        match e {
157	            erc1967::utils::Error::InvalidImplementation(e) => {
158	                Error::InvalidImplementation(e)
159	            }
160	            erc1967::utils::Error::InvalidAdmin(e) => Error::InvalidAdmin(e),
161	            erc1967::utils::Error::InvalidBeacon(e) => Error::InvalidBeacon(e),
162	            erc1967::utils::Error::NonPayable(e) => Error::NonPayable(e),
163	            erc1967::utils::Error::EmptyCode(e) => Error::EmptyCode(e),
164	            erc1967::utils::Error::FailedCall(e) => Error::FailedCall(e),
165	            erc1967::utils::Error::FailedCallWithReason(e) => {
166	                Error::FailedCallWithReason(e)
167	            }
168	        }
169	    }
170	}
171	
172	impl MethodError for Error {
173	    fn encode(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
174	        self.into()
175	    }
176	}
177	
178	/// NOTE: Implementation of [`TopLevelStorage`] to be able use `&mut self` when
179	/// calling other contracts and not `&mut (impl TopLevelStorage +
180	/// BorrowMut<Self>)`. Should be fixed in the future by the Stylus team.
181	unsafe impl TopLevelStorage for UUPSUpgradeable {}
182	
183	/// Interface for a UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard) upgradeable
184	/// contract.
185	pub trait IUUPSUpgradeable: IErc1822Proxiable {
186	    /// Returns the version of the upgrade interface of the contract.
187	    ///
188	    /// NOTE: Make sure to set proper selector in order to make the function
189	    /// compatible with Solidity version.
190	    ///
191	    /// ```rust,ignore
192	    /// #[selector(name = "UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION")]
193	    /// fn upgrade_interface_version(&self) -> String {
194	    ///     self.uups.upgrade_interface_version()
195	    /// }
196	    /// ```
197	    ///
198	    /// # Arguments
199	    ///
200	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
201	    fn upgrade_interface_version(&self) -> String;
202	
203	    /// Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `new_implementation`, and
204	    /// subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`.
205	    ///
206	    /// Note: This primitive does not include an authorization mechanism. To
207	    /// restrict who can upgrade, enforce access control in your contract
208	    /// before delegating to this function.
209	    ///
210	    /// # Arguments
211	    ///
212	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
213	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation contract.
214	    /// * `data` - Additional data to be passed to the new implementation.
215	    ///
216	    /// # Errors
217	    ///
218	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the call is not made through a
219	    ///   valid proxy context.
220	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation address
221	    ///   is invalid or doesn't implement the required interface.
222	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
223	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
224	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
225	    ///   not designed to handle it.
226	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
227	    ///   address.
228	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] to the
229	    ///   new implementation fails.
230	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
231	    ///   [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] fails with a specific reason.
232	    ///
233	    /// # Events
234	    ///
235	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the implementation
236	    ///   is upgraded.
237	    ///

246	/// A contract that implements the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard)
247	/// pattern for upgradeable contracts.
248	///
249	/// # Overview
250	///
251	/// This implementation provides upgradeability functionality for proxy
252	/// contracts while maintaining storage compatibility across upgrades. It
253	/// follows the UUPS pattern defined in [EIP-1822], where the upgrade
254	/// logic is included in the implementation contract rather than the proxy.
255	///
256	/// This Stylus version contains some architectural differences compared to
257	/// Solidity's implementation, while maintaining the same security model and
258	/// upgrade flow.
259	///
260	/// # Design Rationale & Differences from Solidity
261	///
262	/// ## Storage-based Context Detection
263	///
264	/// Solidity often relies on an `immutable` self-address to detect context. In
265	/// Stylus, this contract uses a boolean `logic_flag` stored in a dedicated
266	/// slot:
267	/// - When executing directly on the implementation, the constructor has set
268	///   `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage.
269	/// - When executing via proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), the proxy’s
270	///   storage does not have this flag, so the check reads as `false`.
271	///
272	/// ## Initialization Pattern
273	///
274	/// - Constructor: runs once on implementation deployment, sets `logic_flag`.
275	/// - Runtime initializer: `set_version()` must be invoked via the proxy to
276	///   write this logic’s `VERSION_NUMBER` into the proxy’s storage. This aligns
277	///   the proxy’s version with the logic and enables upgrade paths guarded by
278	///   `only_proxy()`.
279	///
280	/// ## Proxy Safety Checks
281	///
282	/// The [`UUPSUpgradeable::only_proxy`] function ensures that:
283	///
284	/// 1. The call is being made through a `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
285	/// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
286	/// 3. The `VERSION_NUMBER` in implementation equals to the version stored in
287	///    the proxy.
288	///
289	/// **Security Note:** Bypassing these checks could allow unauthorized upgrades
290	/// or break the proxy pattern, potentially leading to storage collisions or
291	/// unauthorized upgrades.
292	///
293	/// # Edge Cases & Pitfalls
294	///
295	/// ## Common Mistakes
296	///
297	/// * The new implementation doesn't expose `set_version()` or the version
298	///   number constant does not increase.
299	/// * Calling upgrade entrypoints directly on the implementation.
300	/// * Using a non-ERC-1967 proxy.
301	/// * Incorrectly implementing `proxiable_uuid()` in derived contracts.
302	///
303	/// ## Security Considerations
304	///
305	/// * Always use the `only_proxy` modifier for upgrade functions
306	/// * Never expose `_upgrade_to_and_call_uups` directly
307	/// * Ensure all storage variables are append-only in upgrades
308	/// * Test upgrades thoroughly on testnet before mainnet deployment
309	///
310	/// # Usage
311	///
312	/// ```rust
313	/// extern crate alloc;
314	///
315	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::utils::uups_upgradeable::UUPSUpgradeable;
316	/// use stylus_sdk::{prelude::*, storage::StorageU256};
317	///
318	/// #[storage]
319	/// #[entrypoint]
320	/// pub struct MyUpgradeableContract {
321	///     // Must include UUPSUpgradeable as the first field
322	///     uups: UUPSUpgradeable,
323	///
324	///     // Your contract's state variables
325	///     value: StorageU256,
326	///     // ...
327	/// }
328	///
329	/// #[public]
330	/// impl MyUpgradeableContract {
331	///     // Call this via the proxy once to align the proxy's version with the logic.
332	///     pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
333	///         self.uups.set_version().map_err(Into::into)
334	///     }
335	///
336	///     // Your contract's functions
337	/// }
338	/// ```
339	///
340	/// [EIP-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
341	/// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
342	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
343	#[storage]
344	pub struct UUPSUpgradeable {
345	    /// Logic version number stored in the proxy contract.
346	    pub version: StorageU32,
347	}
348	
349	#[public]
350	#[implements(IUUPSUpgradeable, IErc1822Proxiable)]
351	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
352	    /// Initializes implementation-only state used for context checks.
353	    ///
354	    /// Sets `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage to indicate
355	    /// a direct (non-delegated) execution context.
356	    ///
357	    /// # Arguments
358	    ///
359	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
360	    #[constructor]
361	    pub fn constructor(&mut self) {
362	        self.logic_flag().set(true);
363	    }
364	
365	    /// Sets the proxy-stored runtime `version` for this logic
366	    /// (initializer-like).
367	    ///
368	    /// Intended to be called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) to
369	    /// record `VERSION_NUMBER` in the proxy’s storage.
370	    ///
371	    /// # Arguments
372	    ///
373	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
374	    ///
375	    /// # Errors
376	    ///
377	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If not called via proxy
378	    ///   `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
379	    /// * [`Error::InvalidVersion`] - If the proxy's stored `version` is greater
380	    ///   than this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`.
381	    ///
382	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
383	    pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
384	        if self.not_delegated().is_ok() {
385	            return Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(
386	                UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {},
387	            ));
388	        }
389	        if self.version.get() > VERSION_NUMBER {
390	            return Err(Error::InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion {
391	                current_version: self.version.get().to(),
392	            }));
393	        }
394	
395	        self.version.set(VERSION_NUMBER);
396	        Ok(())
397	    }
398	}

406	    #[payable]
407	    fn upgrade_to_and_call(
408	        &mut self,
409	        new_implementation: Address,
410	        data: Bytes,
411	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
412	        self.only_proxy()?;
413	        self._upgrade_to_and_call_uups(new_implementation, &data)?;
414

416	            UUPSUpgradeableInterface::setVersionCall {}.abi_encode();
417	        AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
418	            self,

420	            &data_set_version,
421	        )?;
422	
423	        Ok(())
424	    }

427	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
428	    /// Get the logic contract version.
429	    ///
430	    /// # Arguments
431	    ///
432	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
433	    #[must_use]
434	    pub fn get_version(&self) -> U32 {
435	        VERSION_NUMBER
436	    }
437	
438	    /// Get the logic flag from the appropriate storage slot.
439	    ///
440	    /// # Arguments
441	    ///
442	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
443	    #[must_use]
444	    pub fn logic_flag(&self) -> StorageBool {
445	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageBool>(LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT)
446	    }
447	
448	    /// Return the value stored in the logic flag slot.
449	    ///
450	    /// # Arguments
451	    ///
452	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
453	    #[must_use]
454	    pub fn is_logic(&self) -> bool {
455	        self.logic_flag().get()
456	    }
457	
458	    /// Ensures the call is being made through a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
459	    ///
460	    /// Checks:
461	    /// 1. Execution is happening via [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] (checked
462	    ///    via `!self.is_logic()`).
463	    /// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy (implementation slot is
464	    ///    non-zero).
465	    /// 3. The proxy state is consistent for this logic (the proxy-stored
466	    ///    version equals this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`).
467	    ///
468	    /// [`onlyProxy`]: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/c64a1edb67b6e3f4a15cca8909c9482ad33a02b0/contracts/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol#L50
469	    ///
470	    /// # Security Implications
471	    ///
472	    /// This check prevents direct calls to upgrade functions on the
473	    /// implementation contract.
474	    ///
475	    /// Note: This is not a reentrancy guard. Use a dedicated mechanism if
476	    /// reentrancy protection is required.
477	    ///
478	    /// # Edge Cases
479	    ///
480	    /// * Calls from [ERC-1167] minimal proxies are not guaranteed to pass this
481	    ///   check
482	    ///
483	    /// # Arguments
484	    ///
485	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
486	    ///
487	    /// # Errors
488	    ///
489	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If any of the above conditions is
490	    ///   not met
491	    ///
492	    /// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
493	    /// [ERC-1167]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1167
494	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
495	    pub fn only_proxy(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
496	        if self.is_logic()
497	            || Erc1967Utils::get_implementation() == Address::ZERO
498	            || U32::from(self.get_version()) != self.version.get()
499	        {
500	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
501	        } else {
502	            Ok(())
503	        }
504	    }
505	
506	    /// Check that the execution is not being performed through a
507	    /// [`delegate_call`].
508	    ///
509	    /// This allows a function to be callable on the implementing contract
510	    /// but not through proxies.
511	    ///
512	    /// # Arguments
513	    ///
514	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
515	    ///
516	    /// # Errors
517	    ///
518	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the execution is performed via
519	    ///   [`delegate_call`].
520	    ///
521	    /// [`delegate_call`]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
522	    pub fn not_delegated(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
523	        if self.is_logic() {
524	            Ok(())
525	        } else {
526	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
527	        }
528	    }
529	}

539	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
540	    /// Performs an implementation upgrade with a security check for UUPS
541	    /// proxies, and additional setup call.
542	    ///
543	    /// As a security check, [`IErc1822Proxiable::proxiable_uuid`] is invoked
544	    /// in the new implementation, and the return value is expected to be the
545	    /// implementation slot in ERC-1967.
546	    ///
547	    /// # Arguments
548	    ///
549	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
550	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
551	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the new implementation.
552	    ///
553	    /// # Errors
554	    ///
555	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation doesn't
556	    ///   support the required interface or is invalid.
557	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
558	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
559	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
560	    ///   not designed to handle it.
561	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
562	    ///   address.
563	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] to the
564	    ///   new implementation fails.
565	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
566	    ///   [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] fails with a specific reason.
567	    ///
568	    /// # Events
569	    ///
570	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Erc1967Proxy::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the
571	    ///   implementation is upgraded.
572	    ///
573	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
574	    fn _upgrade_to_and_call_uups(
575	        &mut self,
576	        new_implementation: Address,
577	        data: &Bytes,
578	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
579	        let slot = Erc1822ProxiableInterface::new(new_implementation)
580	            .proxiable_uuid(Call::new_in(self))
581	            .map_err(|_e| {
582	                Error::InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
583	                    implementation: new_implementation,
584	                })
585	            })?;
586	
587	        if slot == IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT {
588	            Erc1967Utils::upgrade_to_and_call(self, new_implementation, data)
589	                .map_err(Error::from)
590	        } else {
591	            Err(Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID {
592	                slot,
593	            }))
594	        }
595	    }
596	}

21	/// Automatically computes the ERC-165 interface ID for a trait.
22	///
23	/// Adds an `interface_id` associated function to your trait by XOR-ing all
24	/// method selectors together, following the ERC-165 standard.
25	///
26	/// ## Method naming
27	///
28	/// By default, Rust method names are converted to camelCase for Solidity.
29	/// Use `#[selector(name = "...")]` to override the Solidity function name.
30	///
31	/// ## Examples
32	///
33	/// ### Basic usage
34	///
35	/// ```rust,ignore
36	/// #[interface_id]
37	/// pub trait IErc721 {
38	///     fn balance_of(&self, owner: Address) -> Result<U256, Vec<u8>>;
39	///     fn owner_of(&self, token_id: U256) -> Result<Address, Vec<u8>>;
40	///
41	///     // Function overloading: different Rust names, same Solidity name
42	///     fn safe_transfer_from(
43	///         &mut self,
44	///         from: Address,
45	///         to: Address,
46	///         token_id: U256,
47	///     ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
48	///
49	///     #[selector(name = "safeTransferFrom")]
50	///     fn safe_transfer_from_with_data(
51	///         &mut self,
52	///         from: Address,
53	///         to: Address,
54	///         token_id: U256,
55	///         data: Bytes,
56	///     ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
57	/// }
58	///
59	/// // Now you can use the computed interface ID:
60	/// impl IErc165 for Erc721 {
61	///     fn supports_interface(&self, interface_id: B32) -> bool {
62	///         <Self as IErc721>::interface_id() == interface_id
63	///             || <Self as IErc165>::interface_id() == interface_id
64	///     }
65	/// }
66	/// ```
67	///
68	/// ### Selector collision error
69	///
70	/// The macro will catch duplicate Solidity signatures at compile time:
71	///
72	/// ```compile_fail
73	/// #[interface_id]
74	/// trait BadTrait {
75	///     fn transfer(&self, to: Address, amount: U256);          // transfer(address,uint256)
76	///
77	///     #[selector(name = "transfer")]
78	///     fn send_tokens(&self, recipient: Address, value: U256); // transfer(address,uint256) ❌ collision!
79	/// }
80	/// ```
81	#[proc_macro_attribute]
82	pub fn interface_id(attr: TokenStream, input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
83	    interface_id::interface_id(&attr, input)
84	}
85

# Audit findings review: OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus (baseline v0.3.0)

## Scope and method

- Reports read in full (every page legible; nothing unreadable):
  `2024-10-v0.1.0.pdf` (15 pp., 2024-10-17, audited commit 42c859f),
  `Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit.pdf` (20 pp., 2025-06-17, a67ab70/2350766 crypto, 5ed33dd contracts),
  `Stylus Contracts Library v0.3.0 Audit.pdf` (17 pp., 2025-09-08, 231d4f1 = v0.3.0-rc.1).
- Code baseline: `/tmp/bench/wt/v030` (tag v0.3.0, commit 47ad800). **All paths below are relative to that directory.**
- Limits: the clone is shallow (1 commit), so none of the fix commits/PRs cited by the reports exist locally;
  every verdict comes from reading the v0.3.0 code. No builds or tests were run (read-only). Curve constants,
  P-256 `n/2` and ERC-165 interface IDs were recomputed independently with standalone Python arithmetic.
- Verdicts: FIXED / PARTIAL / NOT FIXED / CANNOT VERIFY, as defined in the task.

## 1. Summary

| Report | Findings | Marked resolved | FIXED | PARTIAL | NOT FIXED | CANNOT VERIFY | Acknowledged (still present at v0.3.0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1.0 | 12 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3 (3) |
| v0.2.0 | 22 | 20 | 17 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 (2) |
| v0.3.0 | 17 | 17 | 15 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Total | 51 | 46 | 38 | 7 | 1 | 0 | 5 (5) |

Resolved-but-not-fully-fixed:
- Substantive: v0.3.0 H-01 (Baby Jubjub generator), v0.3.0 L-03 (UUPS version check is inert),
  v0.2.0 L-09 (`Uint::eq` still exits early), v0.1.0 L-03 (allowance still spent before the `to` check; negligible impact).
- Cosmetic: v0.1.0 N-01 (TODOs), v0.1.0 N-04 ("modifier" wording), v0.2.0 N-09 (typos), v0.2.0 N-01 (`#[must_use]`).

## 2. Findings extracted from the reports

### 2.1 v0.1.0 report (2024-10-v0.1.0.pdf). Report summary: 12 issues, 9 resolved

| Report | ID | Title | Severity | Status | Auditor's description | Fix ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1.0 | M-01 | ERC-721 Does Not Support ERC-165 | Medium | Resolved | ERC721 does not implement `supportsInterface` (required by EIP-721), so marketplaces and integrators cannot detect it as ERC-721. | commit 4106d03 |
| v0.1.0 | L-01 | Incomplete Implementation for checkpoints.rs | Low | Resolved | Only `uint160` checkpoints exist; Solidity also has `uint208`/`uint224` (TODO on line 17). | commit 3b560b3 |
| v0.1.0 | L-02 | Inconsistent Implementations in ERC-721 Extension | Low | Resolved | URI-storage `token_uri()` skips the token-existence check and base-URI concatenation; `Erc721Metadata` exposes `base_uri` and lacks `tokenURI` by default. | commit 47d2d9c |
| v0.1.0 | L-03 | Missing Checks in ERC-20 Implementation | Low | Resolved | `_approve` does not reject a zero owner; `_spend_allowance` writes storage directly, bypassing `_approve`; `transfer_from` spends allowance before `_transfer`'s zero-address checks. | commit 59dafb4 |
| v0.1.0 | L-04 | Public Exposure of pause and unpause Functions | Low | Resolved | `pause`/`unpause` sit in a `#[public]` block, so they are exposed in inheriting contracts' ABI with no access control. | commit af826da |
| v0.1.0 | L-05 | Inconsistent Function Visibility in Burnable Extension | Low | Acknowledged, not fixed (SDK allows one `#[public]` per crate) | ERC-20/ERC-721 burnable `burn`/`burn_from` are not exposed; developers must implement them, unlike other extensions. | none |
| v0.1.0 | L-06 | Inconsistent Implementation Styles | Low | Acknowledged, not fixed (no Solidity-style inheritance) | Consecutive/Permit embed `erc721`/`erc20` and duplicate base code; Capped leaves capping to the user; mixed styles are error-prone. | none |
| v0.1.0 | N-01 | Unaddressed TODOs and FIXMEs | Note | Resolved | TODO/FIXME at ERC-20 `metadata.rs` L59/L73, ERC-721 `enumerable.rs` L11/L71, ERC-721 `mod.rs` L486/L665; remove them or link them to issues. | commit 997fcc0 |
| v0.1.0 | N-02 | Inconsistent Error Types | Note | Acknowledged (standardize in a future release) | Some extensions use associated error types (generic `Vec`), others do not (e.g. the `IERC20` trait). | none |
| v0.1.0 | N-03 | Unnecessary Swap Operation | Note | Resolved | `commutative_hash_pair` swaps `a`/`b` instead of reversing the `hash_pair` arguments. | commit 7c84e68 |
| v0.1.0 | N-04 | Misleading Reference to Modifiers in Pausable Module | Note | Resolved | Docs call `when_not_paused`/`when_paused` "modifiers", which Stylus does not have; reword this and any others. | commit c056473 |
| v0.1.0 | N-05 | Unused Error Message | Note | Resolved | `ECDSAInvalidSignatureLength` is unused (fixed-length params); remove it and the misplaced comment at L189. | commit 6eeb15c |

### 2.2 v0.2.0 report. Report summary: 22 issues, 20 resolved

| Report | ID | Title | Severity | Status | Auditor's description | Fix ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.2.0 | H-01 | Limb Shift Overflow in shr_assign and shl_assign | High | Resolved | `Uint<N>` `<<=`/`>>=` overflow the intra-limb shift when the bit offset is 0 (a shift by 64): panic in debug, wrong result in release. | PR #658, c38b883 |
| v0.2.0 | M-01 | Potential Underflow in ct_rem Function | Medium | Resolved | `ct_rem` uses `ct_num_bits() - 1`, which underflows for a zero dividend and gives wrong results. | PR #667, 36ab98e |
| v0.2.0 | M-02 | Customer [sic] Selectors in Trait With interface_id Attribute Are Not Checked in Implementation | Medium | Acknowledged, will resolve (needs SDK support) | `#[interface_id]` consumes `#[selector]` in traits; nothing forces implementations to use the same selectors, so the ABI can diverge from the trait/interface ID. | none |
| v0.2.0 | L-01 | Verification Functions for Custom Hashing in Merkle Trees Assume Commutative Hashing | Low | Resolved | `verify_with_builder`/`verify_multi_proof_with_builder` hash commutatively; document that custom hashing must be commutative. | PR #674, 6f75f80 |
| v0.2.0 | L-02 | Inconsistent Data Types for carry and borrow Parameters | Low | Resolved | `adc`/`sbb` take a `Limb` carry/borrow while `*_assign` take `bool`; e.g. `borrow = 2` breaks `sbb`'s overflow protection. Use `bool`. | PR #675, cde91fc |
| v0.2.0 | L-03 | Encoding Ambiguity in ct_num_bits Function | Low | Resolved | `ct_num_bits(0)` returns 0; it should return at least 1 bit. | PR #681, e36c292 |
| v0.2.0 | L-04 | Absence of Overflow Check in from_str_hex Function | Low | Resolved | Oversized hex input causes an index-out-of-bounds panic; add an explicit overflow check like `from_str_radix`. | PR #673, a988e2b |
| v0.2.0 | L-05 | Underlying Decimals in Erc20Wrapper Can Be Set Incorrectly | Low | Resolved | The constructor sets the underlying token but `underlying_decimals` must be set manually and can be wrong. | PR #699, add8075 |
| v0.2.0 | L-06 | State Mutability Can Be Restricted in IErc4626 | Low | Resolved | Read-only `IErc4626` methods (`total_assets`, `convert_to_*`, ...) take `&mut self`; use `&self`. | PR #698, 33b15ed |
| v0.2.0 | L-07 | Custom Selectors in Trait With interface_id Allows Unreachable Patterns | Low | Resolved | Traits with duplicate selectors are accepted by `#[interface_id]` and can never be implemented; reject them. | PR #702, b68f7ae |
| v0.2.0 | L-08 | Missing Trait Components in Generated Code From interface_id Macro | Low | Resolved | The regenerated trait drops generic bounds and the `unsafe` qualifier. | PR #705, 184bf10 |
| v0.2.0 | L-09 | Potential Vulnerability in Big Integer Library to Timing Side-Channel Attacks | Low | Resolved | `ct_ge`, `ct_gt`, `cmp` return early, so execution time is not constant. | PR #700, 7ae1021 |

The three reports contain 51 findings. Of the 46 the auditors marked resolved, 38 are really fixed in v0.3.0, 7 are only partly fixed and 1 is not fixed. No PDF page was unreadable. The repo is a shallow clone, so none of the cited fix commits exist locally; every verdict comes from reading the v0.3.0 code, and no tests were run.

| Report | Findings | Marked resolved | FIXED | PARTIAL | NOT FIXED | Acknowledged (still present) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1.0 | 12 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 3 (3) |
| v0.2.0 | 22 | 20 | 17 | 2 | 1 | 2 (2) |
| v0.3.0 | 17 | 17 | 15 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

The v0.3.0 report has no acknowledged or unresolved findings. The 5 acknowledged ones from the earlier reports (v0.1.0 L-05, L-06, N-02; v0.2.0 M-02, N-10) all still exist in v0.3.0.

Marked resolved but NOT FIXED or PARTIAL (paths relative to `/tmp/bench/wt/v030`):
- **v0.3.0 H-01, PARTIAL:** Bandersnatch and Jubjub are now correct (I recomputed the constants). But Baby Jubjub, added in the same PR, has the same defect: its generator is not in the prime-order subgroup (`lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17`).
- **v0.3.0 L-03, PARTIAL:** the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart, because it always compares against a fixed library constant of 1 that users cannot override (`contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436, 495-504`).
- **v0.2.0 L-09, PARTIAL:** the reported comparisons no longer exit early, but `Uint::eq` still does (`lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188`).
- **v0.1.0 L-03, PARTIAL:** two of the three items are fixed. `transfer_from` still spends the allowance before checking the recipient (`contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs:314-324`); this matches Solidity's order and only wastes gas.
- **v0.2.0 N-01, NOT FIXED (low impact):** only `verify` has `#[must_use]`; `verify_multi_proof` and `verify_with_builder` still lack it (`lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181`).
- **v0.1.0 N-01, PARTIAL (cosmetic):** the listed TODOs are gone but many unlinked ones remain (e.g. `contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/flash_mint.rs:17`).
- **v0.1.0 N-04, PARTIAL (cosmetic):** the "modifier" wording remains at `contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:305`.
- **v0.2.0 N-09, PARTIAL (cosmetic):** the named typos are fixed but others remain (e.g. "grater" in `contracts/src/utils/cryptography/ecdsa.rs:85`, `lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:86`).

The v0.2.0 report also has unnumbered Poseidon2 recommendations; none are implemented.

One security observation outside the reports: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars (`lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96`). That matters because the v0.3.0 report expects signing to run off-chain.
